fact: The National Cyber Security Coordination Centre (NC3) is stated to exist and to have developed, with MoCTI, draft sector-specific critical information infrastructure protection plans for energy, health, education and defence and security, presented for validation on 2026-08-26.

The minister told Parliament that the ministry runs public education campaigns in collaboration with NatCA, the National Cyber Security Coordination Centre and mobile operators, so the Centre is stated to exist and operate.

NatCA, the telecom regulator, issued a public notice on 30 July 2026 acknowledging ongoing cybersecurity incidents, saying it coordinates a response and advising the public on precautions; no incident detail is given.

MoCTI's 3 March 2026 notice names the National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre (NC3) as a partner in launching a leadership training, treating it as an existing national body; the training itself is not a fact.
The article states NC3 published an advisory on its website in July 2024 warning of a surge in WhatsApp takeover attacks.

The article reports interviewing NC3, whose Director of Cyber Resilience commented on WhatsApp takeovers, so the national centre was operating in 2026; it also says no national statistics on such takeovers exist.
SierraLoaded reports that Sierra Leone's National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre (NC3) acts through the national computer security incident response team, SL-CSIRT.
NC3, through SL-CSIRT, issued a critical alert reported on 24 October 2026 on two PHP remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, severity 9.2).
ECOWAS reports the National Cyber Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) was officially launched in Freetown on 14 January 2025 at the NC3 headquarters.
